uncertainties: The running header was read only from the top edge of band 1 and the full scan, where it is partly cut off or small. Its pointing is not certain.

blocks.text: יְסוֹדוֹ מֵעָפָר וְסוֹפוֹ לֶעָפָר. בְּנַפְשׁוֹ יָבִיא לַחְמוֹ. מָשׁוּל כַּחֶרֶס הַנִּשְׁבָּר. כְּחָצִיר יָבֵשׁ. וּכְצִיץ נוֹבֵל. כְּצֵל עוֹבֵר. וְכֶעָנָן כָּלֶה. וּכְרוּחַ נוֹשָׁבֶת. וּכְאָבָק פּוֹרֵחַ. וְכַחֲלוֹם יָעוּף:
uncertainties: This continues from the previous page and starts mid-sentence.
There may be a meteg next to the segol under ח in כַּחֶרֶס, and next to the qamats under שׁ in נוֹשָׁבֶת.

blocks.text: וְאַתָּה הוּא מֶלֶךְ אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם:
uncertainties: The heading is printed in very large display type. In אֵל the alef and lamed are joined as one ligature (ﭏ), with a tsere under it.

blocks.text: ח׳ אֵין קִצְבָה לִשְׁנוֹתֶיךָ. וְאֵין קִצָּה (נ״א קֵץ) לְאֹרֶךְ יָמֶיךָ. וְאֵין לְשַׁעֵר מַרְכְּבוֹת כְּבוֹדֶךָ. וְאֵין לְפָרֵשׁ עֵילוּם שְׁמֶךָ. שִׁמְךָ נָאֶה לְךָ וְאַתָּה נָאֶה לִשְׁמֶךָ. וּשְׁמֵנוּ קָרָאתָ בִּשְׁמֶךָ:
uncertainties: ח׳ is a small speaker mark, probably short for חזן (cantor).
I can't tell whether ב in קִצְבָה has a dagesh.
I can't tell whether צ in קִצָּה has a dagesh.
The small abbreviation inside the brackets looks like either נ״א or כ״א. I read it as נ״א ('another version'), so (נ״א קֵץ) is an alternative reading.
עֵילוּם looks like it has a tsere under ע, not the expected hiriq. Please check this against the image.
There may be a meteg in לְפָרֵשׁ.

blocks.text: קו״ח עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ. וְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת שִׁמְךָ עַל מַקְדִּישֵׁי שְׁמֶךָ:
uncertainties: The small speaker mark looks like 'קרח' but is probably קו״ח, meaning קהל וחזן (congregation and cantor).

blocks.text: חזן כְּסוֹד שִׂיחַ שַׂרְפֵי קֹדֶשׁ. הַמַּקְדִּישִׁים שִׁמְךָ בַּקֹּדֶשׁ. דָּרֵי מַעְלָה עִם דָּרֵי מַטָּה קוֹרְאִים וּמְשַׁלְּשִׁים בְּשִׁלּוּשׁ קְדֻשָּׁה בַּקֹּדֶשׁ.
uncertainties: This passage is printed in larger type than the rest of the page.
The last line is stretched to fill the width: the letters of קְדֻשָּׁה are widely spaced. This is a single word.
In בְּשִׁלּוּשׁ, the dagesh in ל is probable but small.

blocks.text: ח׳ כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ. וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל זֶה וְאָמַר.
קו״ח קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ יְיָ צְבָאוֹת מְלֹא כָל־הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ:
uncertainties: The speaker mark is probably קו״ח.
כָל and הָאָרֶץ are printed touching. I think there is a maqaf between them.
There may be a meteg under ה in הָאָרֶץ.

blocks.text: ק׳ כְּבוֹדוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם מְשָׁרְתָיו שׁוֹאֲלִים זֶה לָזֶה אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ לְעֻמָּתָם בָּרוּךְ יֹאמֵרוּ:
uncertainties: ק׳ is probably short for קהל (congregation). This passage is in larger, stretched type.
There may be a meteg in מְשָׁרְתָיו.

blocks.text: ע״ס א״ב ובסוף חתום שם המחבר אלעזר.
uncertainties: This is a tiny, unpointed note centred above the piyyut. The second word of the phrase could be read as וכסוף or ובסוף, because כ and ב look alike in this small type. ובסוף makes sense. The note says the poem is arranged in alphabetical order (ע״ס א״ב, 'according to the order of the alef-bet') and ends with the author's name, אלעזר.

blocks.text: ק׳ וְחַיּוֹת אֲשֶׁר הֵנָּה מְרֻבָּעוֹת כִּסֵּא. בְּמָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים וָשֵׁשׁ מַכְנִיפוֹת כִּסֵּא. גּוֹעֲשׁוֹת בּוֹ בְּסוֹכְכָם פָּנִים בְּפָנִים לַכִּסֵּא. דְּמוּת רָקִיעַ בְּרָאשָׁם נָטוּי לַכִּסֵּא. הוּא כְּעֵין הַקֶּרַח בּוֹ שְׁבִיב כִּסֵּא. וּמִמַּעַל לָרָקִיעַ כְּמַרְאֵה דְּמוּת כִּסֵּא. זָעוֹת בְּלִי לֵאוּת מֵהִיל כִּסֵּא. ח׳ חָשׁוֹת בְּרָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב מֵרְעִישׁוֹת (נ״א מַרְעִישׁוֹת) כִּסֵּא. טָסוֹת כַּבָּזָק וְלֹא מְזִיזוֹת הוֹד כִּסֵּא. יוֹדְעוֹת כִּי כָל מָקוֹם לֹא יָכִיל מְקוֹם כִּסֵּא:
uncertainties: The speaker changes partway through: ח׳ appears before חָשׁוֹת.
In the main text the first word has a tsere under מ (מֵרְעִישׁוֹת). The bracketed alternative has a patah (מַרְעִישׁוֹת). The abbreviation in the brackets is נ״א or כ״א.
לֵאוּת could also be read as לֵאוֹת, because the vowel on the ו is unclear.
I can't tell whether כ in כָל has a dagesh.
There may be a meteg in מְרֻבָּעוֹת.
In בְּסוֹכְכָם, the vowel under the second כ is not certain.
The acrostic runs ו ז ח ט י across the verse openings: וְחַיּוֹת, זָעוֹת, חָשׁוֹת, טָסוֹת, יוֹדְעוֹת. Each of these words begins a line. The piyyut continues on the next page.

blocks.text: 109 Musaph for the New Year 109

his end is dust, at the risk of his life he earns his bread, he is to be compared to a broken potsherd, to dry grass, to a withering flower, to a passing shadow, to a drifting cloud, to a gust of wind, to blown dust and to a fleeting dream.
But Thou art King, O God, living and enduring
uncertainties: Printed in italics.

blocks.text: אין

There is no limit to Thy years and no end to the length of Thy days, one cannot measure the chariots of Thy glory nor fathom the mystery of Thy Name; Thy Name is fitting for Thee and Thou art fitting for Thy Name and our name hast Thou called by Thy Name. Act for Thy Name's sake and sanctify Thy Name upon those who sanctify Thy Name.
כסוד

According to the mystic utterance of the holy Seraphim, who sanctify Thy Name in holiness, those who dwell above and those who dwell below, proclaim three times the threefold sanctification in sanctity, as it is written through Thy prophet, once calls to the other and says:
uncertainties: The word Seraphim is hyphenated across a line break in the source ("Ser-/aphim"). I joined it here.

blocks.text: קדוש
'Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory'.
כבודו
His glory fills the world, His servants ask one of the other: 'Where is the site of His glory?' Those opposite them say: 'Blessed . . .'.

notes: s238 was read from the full scan and all four enlarged bands. s239, which is English only, was read from the full scan alone because it is clear at that size; its four enlarged bands were not opened.

The small marks in the right margin of s238 are speaker labels: ח׳ (probably חזן, cantor), ק׳ (probably קהל, congregation), and what is probably קו״ח (congregation and cantor). The word חזן also appears spelled out.
There are no Shabbat additions, sound sequences, cantillation marks or Hebrew-script German on either page. The only bracketed items are two variant readings marked נ״א.
The English page translates the Hebrew only down to 'Blessed . . .'. There is no English for the piyyut beginning וְחַיּוֹת or for the acrostic note.
The citation for Isaiah 6:3 is my identification. Neither page prints a citation.
